speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; how long have you had these symptoms, and have they appeared anywhere else on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.

The clinical presentation of new-onset blisters and mucosal ulcers in a patient who recently started captopril and stopped meloxicam is highly suggestive of a severe cutaneous adverse reaction to these medications. The hiking history and family history are less relevant to the acute presentation, so I will proceed with a diagnosis based on the temporal relationship to the medication changes.
